001package io.github.ai4ci.functions;
002
003import java.io.Serializable;
004
005import org.immutables.value.Value;
006import org.mariuszgromada.math.mxparser.Argument;
007import org.mariuszgromada.math.mxparser.Expression;
008import org.mariuszgromada.math.mxparser.mXparser;
009
010import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonIgnore;
011import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeInfo;
012import com.fasterxml.jackson.annotation.JsonTypeName;
013import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonDeserialize;
014import com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.annotation.JsonSerialize;
015
016/**
017 * A discrete mathematical function defined by a univariate expression.
018 *
019 * <p>
020 * This interface represents a discrete function that can be evaluated at
021 * integer time points. The function is defined by a univariate mathematical
022 * expression provided as a string, where the variable `t` represents time. The
023 * expression is parsed and evaluated using the mXparser library.
024 *
025 * <p>
026 * Downstream uses include any context where a time‑dependent function is
027 * needed, such as in‑host models or demographic adjustments. Implementations
028 * are commonly generated by Immutables (see {@link ImmutableDiscreteFunction}).
029 *
030 * @author Rob Challen
031 */
032@Value.Immutable
033@JsonSerialize(as = ImmutableDiscreteFunction.class)
034@JsonDeserialize(as = ImmutableDiscreteFunction.class)
035@JsonTypeInfo(use = JsonTypeInfo.Id.NAME)
036@JsonTypeName("function")
037public interface DiscreteFunction extends Serializable, KernelFunction {
038
039        // NB this probably needs a lot of refactoring.
040        // The discrete function should not really be a Kernel function but a
041        // Way of specifying one. The normalisation that happens in
042        // KernelFunction.values()
043        // Does not make particular sense given the traditional meaning of a kernel
044        // function. The output of KernelFunction is strictly enforced between 0 and
045        // 1
046        // which this is not... So I think all sorts of mistakes could happen here.
047        // There is a question about how these are applied to the components of the
048        // RiskModel in update() and whether actually it is appropriate this is a
049        // 0..1 range or ought to be on the logistic scale. The whole thing needs
050        // some hard core testing
051
052        // On the plus side this caches its values already due to the @Value.Derived
053        // annotation of KernelFunction so should be relatively performant.
054
055        /**
056         * A univariate mathematical function as a String containing `t` as the
057         * parameter. Supported expressions are described here:
058         * https://mathparser.org/mxparser-math-collection.
059         *
060         * @return the function expression.
061         */
062        String getFTExpression();
063
064        /**
065         * The parsed expression is derived from the function expression and the time
066         * argument. It is not intended to be set directly and is ignored during JSON
067         * serialization.
068         *
069         * @return the parsed expression derived from the function expression and the
070         *         time argument.
071         */
072        @JsonIgnore @Value.Derived
073        default Expression getParsed() {
074                mXparser.disableUlpRounding();
075                mXparser.disableCanonicalRounding();
076                mXparser.disableAlmostIntRounding();
077                var t = this.getTimeArgument();
078                return new Expression(this.getFTExpression(), t);
079        }
080
081        /**
082         * The following methods are derived from the function expression and are not
083         * intended to be set directly. They are ignored during JSON serialization.
084         *
085         * @return the time argument and the parsed expression derived from the
086         *         function expression.
087         */
088        @JsonIgnore @Value.Derived
089        default Argument getTimeArgument() { return new Argument("t"); }
090
091        /**
092         * Evaluate the function at a given integer time `t`. This method sets the
093         * value of the time argument and then calculates the result using the parsed
094         * expression.
095         *
096         * @param t the time at which to evaluate the function.
097         * @return the result of evaluating the function at time `t`.
098         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the function expression is invalid or
099         *                                  if evaluation fails.
100         * @see #getFTExpression()
101         *
102         */
103        @Override
104        default double rawValue(int t) {
105                var xArg = this.getTimeArgument();
106                xArg.setArgumentValue(t);
107                var result = this.getParsed()
108                        .calculate();
109                return result;
110        }
111
112}
